summary: Iteration 7 — Tested the new chat Integrations system (Zapier-style incoming webhook, ad-hoc api-fetch, saved api_fetch records) + the new 'Create task & assign' button on AI synthesized answers. BACKEND: 10 NEW tests in test_integrations.py covering empty-list, create incoming_webhook (with webhook_url payload), api_fetch validation (400 when config.url missing), public webhook drop (no Authorization header → 200 + message persisted with metadata.integration='incoming_webhook' & metadata.source='Zapier'), invalid token 404, /api-fetch GET success (status_code=200 message body contains bitcoin/usd), /api-fetch 502 on unreachable host (http://localhost:9/no-such-route), DELETE integration + webhook-404 after delete, and list-shows-two regression. Plus 73 prior regression = 83/83 PASS (128.8s). FRONTEND E2E (Amit / demo): Opened TEST_Integrations_a4f2bf chat → 'Integrations' button visible in header (data-testid=open-integrations-btn) → dialog opened (data-testid=integrations-dialog) with all 3 tabs (Active, Add new, Quick API fetch) → 'Add new' incoming_webhook 'Test Zapier UI' created → tab auto-switched to Active list, integration-copy-<id> button visible → 'Quick API fetch' CoinGecko BTC URL with label BTC → Run → dialog closed AND chat got a new ai_system message body '**API fetch · BTC** ... bitcoin' (page text contains both 'bitcoin' and 'API fetch'). The synthesized AI answer message in the chat shows BOTH 'SHOW ALL COMPARISONS · PICK A DIFFERENT BEST' AND 'CREATE TASK & ASSIGN' buttons (data-testid=task-<id>) as required.
critical_code_review_comments: MessageBubble.jsx has TWO elements that both set data-testid=`task-${message.id}` — one for synthesized AI answers (line 165) and one for non-AI user messages (line 197). They never render together (mutually exclusive isAI vs !isAI branches), so it's functionally safe, but reusing the same testid for two semantically different actions ('Create task & assign' from AI answer vs 'Convert to task' from user message) violates testid uniqueness intent and may confuse future test authors. Recommend renaming one to e.g. `aitask-${message.id}` or `tasksrc-${message.id}`.

server.py /chats/{chat_id}/api-fetch wraps the entire HTTP request in a single try/except and raises 502 with the raw exception string ('Fetch failed: {e}'). This is fine, but for httpx timeouts vs connect errors vs SSL errors a more specific status code mapping (e.g., 504 on timeout) and a structured response { error, kind } would let the frontend show better toasts.

/api/webhooks/incoming/{token} updates last_used_at AFTER inserting the message — if the message insert fails, last_used_at is also not updated which is the correct behavior, but the broadcast and the update are not in a transaction. Low risk in practice.

models.IntegrationCreate.config has no validation of inner shape (the route checks 'url' presence imperatively). Consider per-type discriminated unions (IncomingWebhookCreate / ApiFetchCreate) for better API errors.
server.py is now ~1387 lines — splitting into routers (ai_router, chat_router, task_router, integration_router) is still pending from iterations 4-6.

test_inline_task_command.py still crashes at import time if REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL is unset (carried forward from iteration 6). Suggested: read base URL via conftest fixture instead of top-level module code.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on all 4 new UI flows tested

Each holds: 1 deleted incoming_webhook integration, 1 surviving api_fetch saved record (CoinGecko URL), 1 webhook-dropped message ('Order #1234' via Zapier), 1 api-fetch message (CoinGecko BTC response). context_for_next_testing_agent: All 5 integration endpoints are green. The api-fetch endpoint hits real external HTTP — note that CoinGecko occasionally returns 429 (rate limit) but the endpoint still returns 200 and posts the 429 body into chat with metadata.status_code reflecting the upstream code — the *backend test* asserts status_code==200 because CoinGecko was responsive during the run; if a future run sees 429, the test will fail on that single assertion. Consider switching the test target to api.github.com/zen (text, no rate limit for occasional hits) if flakiness arises. Webhook public endpoint /api/webhooks/incoming/{token} is correctly outside the require_user dependency and verified to accept JSON without Authorization. The frontend Integrations button has data-testid=open-integrations-btn, dialog has data-testid=integrations-dialog, tabs are 'Active' / 'Add new' / 'Quick API fetch'. The 'Create task & assign' button on synthesized AI answers uses data-testid=task-<message_id> (shared with the Convert-to-task button on user messages — see code review note).
rca of the issue: N/A — all features behave per spec. The only edge note is the duplicate data-testid on MessageBubble (cosmetic), and CoinGecko rate-limit possibility (test flakiness risk, not a bug).
